# Map VPN descriptors and routing semantics explicitly into OH

## Platform difference

An Android-style shared VPN interface still needs OH-native authorization, tunnel/descriptor lifecycle and routing semantics.

## Implementation

FlClash implements a VpnExtensionAbility, IPC and N-API bridge into a Go core. Its gateway/bypass/gVisor changes survive, but temporary routeAddress and private-route additions are reverted later. Etohos instead orchestrates an EasyTier HAR from its UIAbility, derives prefix length from the core configuration and passes the created TUN descriptor into it.

## Applicability

These are distinct process/lifetime architectures; a shared Dart interface does not imply identical native isolation, socket protection or cancellation behavior.

These observations apply to the pinned project revisions below, studied on 2026-09-30 and backfilled on 2026-10-06. Unspecified SDK/device compatibility remains unknown; this is not a fresh upstream assessment.

## Pitfalls and limitations

Etohos' native HAR is an external local dependency whose internals were not audited. Its per-permission try/catch lets setup continue after denial/errors; this must not be treated as successful authorization. Describe retained routing configuration after the revert, not every historical parser option as active.

## Verification

Test consent/denial, descriptor ownership, route/gateway semantics, self-traffic exclusion, disconnect/reconnect and extension teardown with the intended signing/permissions.

Evidence tier: historical source/diff studies, with commit and path existence rechecked in local Git during this backfill. No application build, dependency resolution, signing, installation or device execution was performed. Proposed checks above are acceptance criteria, not completed tests.
